Use `family = "bernoulli"` for a binary response. Coefficient functions are on the log-odds scale, and `x.var` order controls their labels.

## Repeated observations

The [standalone runnable example](https://github.com/esrakurum/Bayesian-TDMM/blob/main/examples/bernoulli-getting-started.R) generates irregular visits with a baseline and time-varying covariate, fits one dataset with `random_intercept = TRUE`, and saves summaries and plots. From the repository root:

```r
library(TDMM)
source("examples/bernoulli-getting-started.R")
fit <- run_small_bernoulli()
summary(fit)
plot(fit)
plot.trace.tdmm(fit, c("sigma.b", "tau.alpha[1]"))
```

Review chain diagnostics for reconstructed coefficient curves, the random-effect scale, and smoothing parameters. The same `tdmm()` workflow is described in [Getting Started](getting-started.html).

## Independent observations

The Bernoulli simulation helper generates one observation per subject when `random_intercept = FALSE`. For independent observations, time may represent age, time since an event, or time relative to an event. The helper defaults to 2,500 subjects in this setting.

```r
independent_data <- data.gen.tdmm.bern(random_intercept = FALSE, seed = 27181)
fit_independent <- tdmm(independent_data, family = "bernoulli",
                        x.var = "x1", random_intercept = FALSE,
                        control = tdmm_control(seed = 77181))
summary(fit_independent)
plot(fit_independent)
```
